New commentary today from SoftBank on Elon Musks post 4 days ago:

“SoftBank is defaulting on their turbine orders”

Analyst Question: “Any comment on that?”

SoftBank CFO Yoshimitsu Goto: “this is simply not correct at all. There is no such default”

This also mirrors what $GE CEO Scott Strazik stated about seeing no procurement cancellations or counterparty financing difficulties.

Pretty damaging allegations about the company financing $SPCX competitor (OpenAI + Stargate).

I wonder if there’s any more nuance these claims or if it’s false.
Serenity @aleabitoreddit · 7 Nov 2026, 19:04 SGT
Some industry commentary regarding a few claims recently on memory + Softbank Turbine defaulting.

- On claims that LTAs are "meaningless while prices fall":

$MU: "strategic customer agreements cannot be unilaterally canceled. Customers are obligated to pay for their committed volumes whether they take delivery or not"

"These are take or pay agreements and there are no contractual outs for our customers from these agreements"

Regarding historical contracts breaking: "These LTAs that we used to have never had any binding terms." The new SCAs contain extensive contractual obligations

Regarding Elon's claims on Softbank defaulting on Turbines:

Question from Morgan Stanley to $GE Vernova CEO on whether they see cancellations or financing difficulties with counterparties on their turbine orders:

“No… we are not”

TLDR:
- Micron states LTAs/SCAs are noncancellable take/pay (where counterparties are hyperscalers). And that these types are different from historical memory cancellations.

- On Softbank turbine orders, GE Vernova CEO Scott Strazik said it wasn't seeing customer financing disruptions, requests to exit turbine reservations, or slowdowns.

Maybe Elon's claims are more narrow, but should be evaluated more closely given competitive interests vs. Softbank/OpenAI.

If you look at CW laser ASPs for AI data centers, the pricing differences are pretty substantial:

70mW: ~$3–4
100mW: ~$4–6 (Source Photonics channel checks).

With some premiums apparently going up to $7-$9 range with the recent shortage for pluggables.

120–150mW NPO: ~$15–20
350mW UHP CW: ~$40 (Nomura)
400mW UHP CW for NPO/CPO: ~$50–75 (Mizuho)

With former communication laser chips going from 20-50 cents.

The pricing and gross margins of these players go up with each architectural shift (60%+ for CPO lasers).

And go up even more depending how far down the stack you go (selling ELSFP was ~2.5x revenue content)

In terms of how I see the landscape now:

- $COHR is probably the best risk adjusted laser player now, for people who don't like uncertainty. Their new $20B LTA is very substantial.

- $LITE pretty negative now given the valuation overhang from $MRVL acquisition. Operationally very opsitive.

- $AAOI has extreme demand visibility (likely $6-$9B in new LTAs from just 1 quarter), but credible execution uncertainty.

They've also been focusing on pluggables + bottlenecked by DSPs, rather focusing on UHP CPO laser merchant markets.

But I think if markets see a new $5B-$7B LTA that they're in late stage discussion for... and see the $4.4B MC. Pretty sure that's a catalyst for recovery.

The demand doesn't disappear but timeline shifts back a few months.

AOI also signaled DSP as the main bottleneck, last quarter it was TIAs, so other different component players that are interesting.

- $SIVE has extreme capacity expansion (300m laser capacity targeted in total).

The economic implications that they won't disclose are likely enormous relative to their MC, even if they sell $3 70mW lasers to China pluggable players.

But there's a qualification uncertainty to fill the gap,
that markets have punished the company for. Especially when management communication amplifies uncertainty, despite the ongoing shortage.

Right now entire AI trade is going up and down together though.
Habesha Tech Bro @HabeshaTechBro · 10 Nov 2026, 14:22 SGT
One nuance worth adding for the semi specialists reading the $AAOI section:

The 720M to 1.44B annual diode figure off the 180,000/year Yunnan Germanium 4-inch wafer contract reflects gross standard pluggable die candidates. Once you apply real-world III-V epitaxy,facet-coating, and 5,000-hour burn-in yields (~45% to 55% net known-good dies), factor in dual-use export license buffers, and account for the ~5x die-area penalty on 300mW to 400mW CPO cavities, $AAOI's net shippable output scales toward ~180M to 300M+ high-speed lasers per year as Texas Phase 2 ramps.

Roughly 80M to 95M of those net dies get absorbed internally just feeding $AAOI's 1M/month transceiver target, leaving ~100M to 200M+ merchant diodes for external buyers inside a 650M to 1B+ combined scale-out and scale-up market. Even if both $AAOI and $SIVE hit full utilization in 2028, merchant Western supply stays structurally short.

Lukas Kafka @Kafka7invest · 10 Nov 2026, 05:06 SGT
$SNAP
Open Letter to Evan Spiegel @evanspiegel
Chief Executive Officer, Snap Inc.

November 9, 2026

Evan Spiegel
Chief Executive Officer
Snap Inc.
3000 31st Street
Santa Monica, CA 90405

Dear Mr. Spiegel,
As a long-term shareholder of Snap Inc., I write to respectfully urge a significant increase in the company’s share repurchase program. While Snap has made meaningful progress in revenue growth, profitability, and free cash flow generation, the ongoing dilution from stock-based compensation (SBC) continues to exert a material negative drag on per-share value for owners.

I specifically request that quarterly share buybacks exceed the dilution caused by SBC each quarter. Doing so would produce a net reduction in the total share count on both a quarterly and annual basis. With common shares outstanding plus shares underlying stock-based awards currently exceeding 1.93 billion and continuing to grow, systematically shrinking the share base is essential to translating operating improvements into lasting shareholder returns.

Reducing shares outstanding directly improves earnings per share (EPS) and free cash flow per share. The same absolute earnings and free cash flow are divided among fewer shares, mechanically increasing these key metrics and compounding value for remaining shareholders over time. This approach also strengthens the balance sheet’s efficiency without requiring incremental operating improvements beyond those already underway.

Warren Buffett has long argued that companies should repurchase shares when they trade below intrinsic value relative to their financial fundamentals. At current prices, Snap appears undervalued relative to its growing free cash flow, user base, and improving margins. Deploying capital into buybacks at these levels would be accretive, increase ownership for long-term holders, and align capital allocation with the interests of patient shareholders—precisely the framework Buffett endorses.

I urge the Board and management to adopt a disciplined, ongoing buyback policy that prioritizes net share count reduction. Such a commitment would demonstrate confidence in Snap’s intrinsic value and reward those who have invested for the long term.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Long-Term Shareholder
Snap Inc.

James E. Thorne @DrJStrategy · 10 Nov 2026, 08:30 SGT
The Data Center Buildout Is Not Dead

The Senate’s 73-25 vote to advance the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act undercuts the claim that rapid data center expansion is politically finished.

With White House support and President Trump publicly backing the measure as a way to unleash energy production and protect ratepayers, the bill both raises costs for operators and clears the largest practical obstacle to new capacity: the inability to build power and transmission on a workable timeline.

Under the legislation, large loads of roughly 20 megawatts or more must cover the full incremental cost of the generation, transmission, and distribution upgrades built to serve them. Ratepayers are shielded from cost shifting, and states gain additional tools to impose collateral or other requirements. Modeling suggests this could meaningfully increase the retail power price faced by data centers and add roughly 10 percent to the annualized cost of a gigawatt-scale facility. Those numbers are real, and some marginal projects will be repriced or delayed.

They are not fatal. The same bill shortens federal environmental reviews, limits the window for legal challenges, strengthens project certainty, and expands federal transmission siting authority after a defined state review period. The binding constraint on data center growth has not been the willingness of capital to fund servers; it has been the multi-year wait for reliable power. Faster permitting of generation and transmission addresses that bottleneck directly.

Higher power costs and clearer cost allocation will push some developers toward co-located generation or more selective site selection. That is an adjustment, not a shutdown. The combination of ratepayer protections, accelerated infrastructure deployment, and explicit Trump administration support is more likely to sustain the buildout than to end it. The political signal is that Washington is prepared to let the projects proceed, provided the incremental costs fall on the operators rather than on everyone else.

good point by Matt, perhaps obvious for PMs

I like to transition my /opportunity workflow straight into grilling so that the whole thread from “these are the problems people have, let’s solve this branch” to “here’s how we solve this” is contextualized
Matt Pocock @mattpocockuk · 10 Nov 2026, 04:22 SGT
One tip to improve your grilling

Instead of talking about the 'what', try explaining more of the 'why'.

BAD: "I want to build an analytics panel for admins with graphs and filters"

GOOD: "Admins can't currently see an overview of the important data in the app"

If you start by explaining your proposed solution, the agent will stick to it. It'll assume all the important stuff is settled, and just grill you on implementation.

But if you describe the problem, you'll give the agent license to be more creative.

You'll end up with a much deeper, better conversation.

The scale of Big Tech's AI future financial obligations is extraordinary:

Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, Anthropic, Microsoft, $MSFT, Amazon, $AMZN, Oracle, $ORCL, and Nvidia, $NVDA, have disclosed a combined $4.49 trillion in off-balance-sheet obligations.

These include future lease payments that have not yet commenced, data-center commitments, equipment purchases, and other contractual obligations.

Alphabet accounts for the largest amount, at $1.08 trillion, followed by Anthropic, at $865 billion, and Meta, at $810 billion.

By comparison, their combined on-balance-sheet obligations total just $758 billion, consisting of long-term debt and existing lease liabilities.

This means off-balance-sheet commitments are nearly 6 times larger than their on-balance-sheet obligations.

In total, these 7 tech companies face ~$5.25 trillion in combined financial obligations.

The AI infrastructure race is facing enormous future financial commitments.

amit@amitisinvesting
05:42 SGT quoteInvesting
Let me say out loud what I think everyone is feeling right now…

Jensen was the poster child for a CEO who didn’t get caught up in these types of controversies.

He is the last person you would think could get caught up in something like this.

When it comes to the AI revolution, he is at the center of it. Without NVIDIA, there is no AI revolution. In many respects, he has been emblematic of American capitalism over the past few years. A dishwasher at Denny’s had an idea and turned it into a $5T company.

Everyone simply thought Jensen was above these types of things.

I don’t even want this to be about a rich powerful man cheating on his wife…we have heard this story over and over again. That isn’t to normalize it as being okay, but it’s not really shocking.

However, the broader issue here is what infidelity implies about someone’s character. You can make many excuses to justify it, but we all know that infidelity is not a good thing. There is a lack of morality involved when it comes to cheating.

When you are the CEO of a $5T company, the question now emerges: if you can lie to your wife, can you also lie about other things…like China’s access to your technology?

I don’t really know what to think. My gut tells me that Jensen has acted ethically in most fronts when it comes to business, but I also know that to build a $5T company, the lines around ethics can blur easily. A framework for being able to make sense of and justify your actions is very, very important and we all simply don’t know if this affair will result in anything bad in regards to America’s national security with China.

I don’t think this is good for the stock market or the AI trade. There will now be investigations and concerns around Nvidia and Nvidia is in control of how all the semis do. I also think this story may have leaked last week and that’s part of why we saw such a massive de-risking by institutions.

I do think there is a world where the market moves beyond this, especially if the investigation doesn’t show any meaningful compromised intelligence. I also think the public will be willing to forgive Jensen, at the end of the day he is a human and infidelity has obviously been part of many marriages, much less such a high profile one.

This is just a really weird moment and not something I ever expected from Jensen. It will now be up to the market to decide how important and meaningful this is when it comes to where the AI trade goes.

The global rate hike cycle is accelerating:

~45% of global central banks have raised interest rates over the last 3 months, the largest total in 3 years.

This proportion has surged +40 percentage points since March.

By comparison, between 2024 and March 2026, more central banks were cutting rates than raising them.

Furthermore, global central banks have delivered 42 rate hikes over the last 6 months, the largest number since late 2023.

This figure has quadrupled over the last 7 months and is comparable to the rate hike cycle seen in 2019.

The global monetary tightening cycle is gaining momentum.

BREAKING: The US unemployment rate has remained below 5.0% for 62 consecutive months, its 2nd-longest streak on record.

This trails only the 64-month stretch recorded during the 1960s and 1970s.

This is also 20 months longer than the 42-month streak that ended during the 2020 pandemic.

The current run began in September 2021, when the unemployment rate fell to 4.7%, from 5.1% in August 2021.

To put this into perspective, the unemployment rate has averaged 5.6% since the start of the century.

The US job market is still remarkably resilient.

History says last week's drop was a buying opportunity.

On Thursday, the S&P 500 declined -4.4%, its largest daily drop since April 2025.

Before that day, the index recorded 56 one-day declines of at least -4.0% since 1952.

Following such drops, the S&P 500 has gained +1.0% on average over the next week.

By comparison, its average weekly return across all periods has been +0.2%.

Over the next month, the index has averaged a gain of +2.0%, compared with +0.8% across all periods.

Over the following 3 months, the S&P 500 has averaged +6.7%, more than triple the historical average of +2.2%.

History suggests the market is set for a meaningful rebound.

23:52 SGTInvesting
Various commentary from Qualcomm, Arm, to Meta executives this week during the AI selloff:

$LITE CEO: "You had a comment from the CEO of $IREN and I'd second that. There's a massive disconnect in what we're seeing in our demand books.

And what the markets are showing. And yet you're seeing a massive, massive selloff." (Fri, Nov 6)

$AMD CEO CNBC: "We're at the very beginning of the adoption cycle, where people can see where AI and superintelligence will take us"

"We are seeing demand being higher than supply" (Wed, Nov 4)

$ARM CEO regarding a debate whether AI infrastructure spending is about to peak:

"I think in some states where it gets harder, other states may pick it up to make it easier, but I do believe strongly that if the US hesitates in any way shape performance in terms of data center buildout...

"The rest of the world is ready and willing. There is just huge demand for this capacity. And I think globally the US really wants to be able to compete against China. China is not slowing down at all." (Thu, Nov 5)

$APLD CEO: Bank construction lending, project financing and bond markets remain available, although interest rates and credit spreads have risen

"The big risk is delivering on time." "The demand picture is extremely robust." (Mon, Nov 2)

$QCOM CEO: "It's not demand bound. It's a supply bound."

"We're short on wafers, we're short on substrate, we're short on assembly. Everything is short because demand is very, very high."

"I think what the market is reacting to is what is the speed of the compute build out."

$META on political risk: "We did have a governor that won last night who did make data centers a big part of the platform.

Say as soon as we get past the inauguration, let's meet because we don't want to lose this investment in our town. We don't want these jobs to go elsewhere." (Wed, Nov 4)

Even politicians campaigning against data centers are negotiating. But Meta's president also emphasized that starting new US DCs will become more difficult.

TLDR:
-> Extremely bullish commentary from accelerator players, networking, and semi companies
-> DC developers report strong pricing/demand, but increasingly emphasize financing, permitting and execution risks (more cautious)
-> Politicians that previously campaigned against DCs are showing cooperation

There's an important difference between demand disappearing and demand being delayed by the inability to build fast enough.

Despite the severity of the selloff, I'm not seeing evidence of widespread AI demand destruction in commentary.

महाराष्ट्राचे मुख्यमंत्री श्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस जी यांनी लोहारी सावंगा गावात (नरखेड, नागपूर) शेतकऱ्यांसोबत दिवाळी साजरी केली आणि त्यांनी अरुणाबाई आणि रामभाऊ बालपांडे यांच्या घरी मुक्काम ही केला, ही त्यांची कृती मनाला स्पर्श करणारी आहे. महाराष्ट्रातील एनडीए सरकार शेतकऱ्यांसाठी संवेदनशीलतेने कार्य करत आहे आणि त्यांच्या कल्याणासाठी प्रयत्नशील आहे, हे या कृतीतून अधोरेखित होते.
Devendra Fadnavis @Dev_Fadnavis · 8 Nov 2026, 03:07 SGT
शेतकऱ्यांच्या डोळ्यांतील अश्रू पुसता आले, हीच माझ्यासाठी खरी दिवाळी!

हेमाडपंथी शिवमंदिराचा ऐतिहासिक वारसा आणि कार नदीमुळे लाभलेले निसर्गसौंदर्य अशा वैशिष्ट्यांनी समृद्ध असलेल्या नागपूर जिल्ह्यातील लोहारी सावंगा या गावी आज शेतकरी बांधवांसमवेत दिवाळी साजरी करण्याचे सौभाग्य प्राप्त झाले. दुष्काळाचा सामना करणाऱ्या बळीराजाचे दुःख, त्याच्या व्यथा आणि कुटुंबाच्या भविष्याची चिंता जाणून घेताना मन भरून आले. आज मी येथील शेतकरी अरुणाबाई बालपांडे आणि रामभाऊ बालपांडे यांच्या घरी मुक्कामी आहे. बालपांडे कुटुंबाने अत्यंत आपुलकीने केलेल्या स्वागताने मन अक्षरशः भारावून गेले आहे. त्यांच्या प्रेमात, जिव्हाळ्यात आणि आपलेपणात एक विलक्षण भावनिक ओलावा आहे.

देशभरात दिवाळीचा उत्साह असताना राज्यातील शेतकरी मात्र चिंतेत आहे. निसर्गाच्या अवकृपेमुळे करपलेली पिके, निर्माण झालेली आर्थिक विवंचना, मुलांच्या शिक्षणाची चिंता त्यांच्या मनात आहे. लोहारी सावंगा येथील शेतकऱ्यांशी या विषयांवर संवाद साधला, त्यांच्या अडचणी जाणून घेतल्या, तेव्हा त्यांच्या चेहऱ्यावरचा ताण हळूहळू निवळताना अनुभवला. "साहेब, तुम्ही थेट आमच्या गावात आलात, आमच्या सुख-दुःखात सहभागी झालात, यातच आमचे अर्धे दुःख हलके झाले," हे त्यांचे शब्द मनाला स्पर्शून गेले.

माझ्यासाठी महाराष्ट्रातील प्रत्येक शेतकऱ्याचे पीक म्हणजे केवळ उत्पादन नाही, तर ते त्याच्या संपूर्ण कुटुंबाने वर्षभर केलेल्या कष्टांचे, त्यागाचे आणि स्वप्नांचे प्रतीक आहे. प्रत्येक पिकामागे कुटुंबाच्या भविष्याची आशा असते आणि प्रत्येक हंगामामागे समृद्धीचे स्वप्न असते. निसर्गाच्या अनिश्चिततेमुळे जेव्हा पीक उद्ध्वस्त होते तेव्हा शेतकऱ्यांच्या भविष्यावरही संकट येते. आज हे दुःख जवळून अनुभवले. म्हणूनच, केवळ मंत्रालयातील बैठका, निर्णय, योजना किंवा आर्थिक सहाय्यापुरते मर्यादित न राहता, बळीराजाच्या शेजारी बसून त्याच्या अडचणी जाणून घेणे, त्याचे अश्रू पुसणे आणि त्याला पुन्हा उभारी देण्यासाठी आधाराचा हात देणे, हा माझा प्रामाणिक प्रयत्न आहे.

रब्बी पिकांचे नुकसान टाळण्यासाठी कोणत्या उपाययोजना करता येतील, याबाबत शेतकऱ्यांशी चर्चा केली. दुष्काळी परिस्थितीच्या पार्श्वभूमीवर शक्य असेल त्या ठिकाणी विंधन विहिरी घेण्यास परवानगी देण्यात येईल. काटोल आणि नरखेड परिसरात संत्र्यासह मोसंबीचे मोठ्या प्रमाणावर उत्पादन घेतले जाते. मात्र, निर्यातीसमोरील नव्या आंतरराष्ट्रीय आव्हानांमुळे शेतकऱ्यांना नुकसान सहन करावे लागत आहे. या पार्श्वभूमीवर नागपूरमधील मिहान प्रकल्पाच्या माध्यमातून संत्री आणि मोसंबीवर प्रक्रिया करण्यासाठी मोठा प्रकल्प उभारण्याचे नियोजन आहे. शेतकरी अडचणीत येऊ नये यासाठी आवश्यक ती खबरदारी घेतली जाईल.

यावेळी मंत्री चंद्रशेखर बावनकुळे, आमदार डॉ. आशिष देशमुख व इतर मान्यवर उपस्थित होते.

$NBIS $MU $LITE $SNDK $NVDA

This is a great way to visualize Thursdays, Nov 5, carnage.

TL;DR:

The selling was about positioning.

The businesses didn’t change on Thursday, and once everyone has de-risked this hard, the next big flow is them buying back... Don’t expect a V-shaped bounce on Monday, but we’re closer to the bottom than to the top.

Here’s more detail on what happened:

+ Hedge funds cut their net bets 5% in a single day, one of the five biggest drops since 2010. Their net exposure is now in the lowest 10% of the last 16 years.

+ Since June they’ve shrunk their books by about 11%, the most in at least a decade.

+ They’re now underweight AI relative to the market, even though AI is still 32% of what they hold.

+ Leveraged ETFs had to sell $57B of stock, the biggest rebalancing on record going back to 2007.

+ Retail dumped the second-most in the first 90 minutes since 2016.

+ Everything is starting to move together, which usually means the de-risking is spreading.
Morgan Stanley Derivatives @MgnStnlyDerivs · 7 Nov 2026, 02:13 SGT
Thursday, November 5th, was a day of extremes:

•US long/short Hedge Fund net leverage declined by 5% day over day, the 5th largest single-day decline since 2010. Net leverage is now in the bottom decile since 2010.^
•Long/short fund active gross flow since June has amounted to a -10.7% reduction relative to their gross market value at the end of June, the most in at least 10 years.^
•Hedge Funds are now underweight AI stocks* relative to market cap weights, but AI is still a very large percent of absolute exposures at 32%.^
•Levered ETFs had the largest amount to sell on data going back to 2007, bringing $57bn of US equity supply.
•Retail selling of US equities in the first 90 minutes, based on MS QDS estimates using public data, was the second largest going back to 2016.
•Equities are now starting to trade in a more correlated fashion, often signaling that risk reduction is broadening out.

^Sourced from MS Prime Brokerage.
*AI stocks defined as the constituents of the MSXXAI Index, made up of AI tech beneficiaries, AI power names, and key hyperscalers

BREAKING: US nonfarm labor productivity rose at a +3.5% annualized in Q3 2026, its largest increase since Q3 2025.

This also marks its 3rd consecutive quarterly improvement.

Nonfarm business output, which excludes the impact of government spending, surged at a +3.7% annualized rate, the strongest growth rate since Q3 2025.

Hourly compensation rose at a +2.9% annualized rate.

As productivity growth outpaced hourly compensation, unit labor costs, which measure labor costs per unit of output, declined -0.7% last quarter, the first quarterly decline since Q2 2025.

This largely a product of companies investing heavily in AI, software, and equipment to improve efficiency, increase output, and contain labor expenses.

AI is catalyzing a major US productivity surge.
